images.caption: East Fayette Street, Baltimore. The tower was built by Jacob Wolfe in 1828 when it was the tallest building in the US. Molten lead was dropped from a platform at the top of the tower, through a sieve-like device, into a vat of cold water at the bottom of the tower[3] to produce "drop shot" for shotguns. It closed in 1898 and was saved for the city in 1928 and is now a museum.
images.alt: East Fayette Street, Baltimore. The tower was built by Jacob Wolfe in 1828 when it was the tallest building in the US. Molten lead was dropped from a platform at the top of the tower, through a sieve-like device, into a vat of cold water at the bottom of the tower[3] to produce "drop shot" for shotguns. It closed in 1898 and was saved for the city in 1928 and is now a museum.

images.caption: This is the basin at the end of the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, looking north toward the end of the canal. Guard lock #8 is at the end of the channel on the left. Interstate Highway 68 / US 40 / US 220 runs on that bridge in the background. The Cumberland Masonic Temple and the Emmanuel Episcopal Church are visible to the left, beyond the highway bridge. The Western Maryland Station is just visiable (brick building, center of picture) beyond the highway bridge. Shops at Canal Place are to the right of the basin. Potomac River is to the left, just beyond the flood wall.
